Agent recipes

An avatar earns its place when it shows what the agent is doing. These recipes wire one to a chat turn: listening, thinking, streaming the reply with lip-sync, tool calls, errors and rest.

A turn, step by step#

Your agent is…CallThe bot
waiting for inputsetState('default')looks around, blinks
watching the user typesetState('listening'), lookAt(input)leans in, eyes on the box
waiting for the first tokensetState('thinking'), set({ status: 'typing' })eyes up, thought bubble, typing badge
streaming the answersay(chunk, { append: true })mouth follows the words
running a toolsetState('working'), set({ status: 'loading' })busy bounce, spinner badge
donesetState('success'), set({ status: 'done' })a happy hop
failedsetState('error'), react('worried')frowns, shakes its head
idle for a whilesetState('sleeping')dozes off

Shortcut: status: 'auto' picks the badge from the state for you, and mood: 'auto' lets the resting face follow how the conversation is going.

Stream an LLM into say()#

Most chat APIs stream the reply as text chunks. Hand each chunk to say() with append: true and the mouth keeps going for as long as text keeps coming; await the last call to know when it has finished talking.

import { createBot } from '@kucukkanat/bots';

const bot = createBot('#agent', { type: 'clover', size: 96, status: 'auto', mood: 'auto' });
const input = document.querySelector('#prompt');

input.addEventListener('input', () => bot.setState(input.value ? 'listening' : 'default'));
input.addEventListener('focus', () => bot.lookAt(input));
input.addEventListener('blur', () => bot.lookAt(null));

async function ask(question, onText) {
  bot.lookAt(null);
  bot.setState('thinking');
  try {
    const res = await fetch('/api/chat', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({ question }) });
    const reader = res.body.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream()).getReader();
    let speaking = Promise.resolve();
    for (;;) {
      const { value, done } = await reader.read();
      if (done) break;
      onText(value);                                  // show it in your chat UI
      speaking = bot.say(value, { append: true });    // and say it
    }
    await speaking;
    bot.setState('success');
  } catch (err) {
    bot.setState('error');
    bot.react('worried');
    throw err;
  }
}

The same works for any SDK that gives you an async iterator of text:

bot.setState('thinking');
for await (const text of stream.textStream) bot.say(text, { append: true });

wpm sets the speaking pace (words per minute). If your UI reveals text at a fixed pace, use the same pace for both so the mouth and the words line up.

Without say()#

On versions without say(), or when you'd rather not lip-sync, the speaking state makes up its own chatter. Feature-detect to support both:

if (typeof bot.say === 'function') await bot.say(reply);
else { bot.setState('speaking'); await revealText(reply); }
bot.setState('success');

Tool calls#

agent.on('tool_start', (tool) => { bot.setState('working'); bot.set({ status: 'loading' }); });
agent.on('tool_end', () => { bot.setState('thinking'); bot.set({ status: 'typing' }); });

Voice and text-to-speech#

If your agent talks out loud, let the audio drive the mouth instead of the text. speak() takes a mic stream, an <audio> element or any Web Audio node:

const audio = new Audio(ttsUrl);
bot.speak(audio);       // mouth follows the sound, state becomes 'speaking'
await audio.play();
audio.onended = () => bot.speak();   // back to the state it was in

With viseme timings from your TTS provider, drive the mouth yourself with bot.setVoice(level), 0 closed to 1 wide.

Rest between turns#

let nap;
const rest = () => { clearTimeout(nap); nap = setTimeout(() => bot.setState('sleeping'), 60_000); };
bot.on('state', (e) => { if (e.state === 'default') rest(); });

A crew of agents#

For multi-agent apps, give every agent a stable look from its id, and let them notice each other:

for (const agent of agents) {
  createBot(agent.el, { identity: agent.id, size: 48, social: true, status: 'auto' });
}

Share a whole crew as a link with a crew page: DNA codes in the URL, no server.

Accessibility#

  • Give each avatar a label; the canvas is an image named after it and its state, e.g. “Clover, thinking”.
  • The avatar is decoration for what your chat UI already says. Keep the reply text in the DOM, in a role="log" region.
  • With prefers-reduced-motion, avatars hold each state's still pose.
